summary: Elevated 5xx "error-floor" observed when priority-shed policy engages causing downstream runtime failures
description:
Issue summary: Beginning ~2026-03-14 03:20 UTC we observed a persistent, elevated 5xx error floor across multiple tenants in prod-us-east correlated with the priority-shedding policy activating. Impact: Customers experienced ~3-8% baseline 5xx for ~40 minutes; several long-lived streaming sessions were terminated with 502/503. Environment: prod-us-east dedicated pool, autoscaler recently applied updated scale-down cooldown. Observed behavior: When aggregate queue length crossed the configured 'shed_threshold' the API gateway began returning 429s and runtimes began hitting internal circuit-breakers; lower-priority tenant requests then escalated to 5xx (502/503) instead of graceful queueing. This looks like an interaction between priority-shed, in-flight request handoff, and runtime prefetch/kv-cache eviction. Steps to reproduce (approx): 1) Simulate sustained mixed-priority load targeting dedicated pool; 2) drive in-proxy queue length above shed_threshold; 3) observe gateway 429s followed by runtime 5xx for lower-priority tenants. Logs/snippets: "[03:22:11 UTC] apigw: conn=xyz priority=low queued=121 shed=1 -> 429"
"[03:22:14 UTC] runtime: thrash detected prefetch_evictions=78 kvcache_misses=0.42 err=runtime_watchdog_reset"
"[03:22:20 UTC] runtime: returning upstream 502 client_conn=abc tenant=nimblechat"
Related signals: spike in autoscaler scale-down events (cooldown window visible), increased runtime watchdog resets, and priority-shed metrics (shed_count) triggered around same time.
investigation_notes: 03:30 UTC - SRE triage: confirmed correlated uptick in shed_count metric on prod-us-east dedicated pool.
03:45 UTC - Hypothesis A: scale-down cooldown shortened available warm workers which increased cold starts and caused runtimes to exceed CPU/GPU affinity, triggering watchdog resets leading to 5xx.

04:00 UTC - Hypothesis B: priority-shed handshake returned 429s to clients but left a fraction of hybrid stream requests in limbo at the router -> runtime boundary, causing duplicated retries and runtime overload.
04:10 UTC - Collected runtime core logs and stack traces for three affected workers; two show repeated 'gpu-kernel-fallback' followed by 'prefetch-stall' messages.
04:30 UTC - Reproduced locally with a load generator (mixed priorities) and confirmed 5xx elevation when shed_threshold < 100 and scale-down cooldown is < 120s.
Linked telemetry: Grafana dashboard 'dedicated/pool/us-east/error-floor' and SLO alerts fired (alert id: SLO-6821).
comments: Aisha Patel (Support) 03:40 UTC: Customer NimbleChat reporting intermittent 502s for low-priority streams; impacting UX for non-paying sandbox users but primary product flows unaffected.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 03:50 UTC: I see the same shed_count surge. Pulling autoscaler logs and will check recent config change; assigning to runtime on-call as well.
Lina Gomez (runtime-oncall) 04:12 UTC: Runtime shows watchdog resets and 'prefetch stall' during reproduction. Suspect interaction with the new prefetch eviction threshold rolled out last week.

Marco Ruiz (SRE) 04:40 UTC: Temporary mitigation applied - raised shed_threshold by 2x for the affected dedicated pool and extended autoscaler scale-down cooldown to 180s. Early signal: 5xx floor reduced to ~0.5%.
NimbleChat Support Rep (customer) 05:05 UTC: Confirmed decrease in 502s, thank you — seeing improved stability on their lower-priority lanes. Need ETA for a permanent fix.
Marco Ruiz (SRE) 05:30 UTC: Next steps documented below; we will prepare a targeted runtime patch and coordinate a non-disruptive rollout. Linking PR once ready.
workaround: Temporary: increased 'shed_threshold' by 2x for prod-us-east dedicated pool and extended autoscaler scale-down cooldown to 180s. This reduces immediate 5xx floor but increases queueing for low-priority traffic. Recommended for customers who were impacted: pin critical routes to higher priority or dedicated smaller capacity until fix is rolled out.
permanent_fix_plan: 1) Runtime change: make priority-shed handshake idempotent and ensure router clears in-flight state when shedding returns 429. 2) Autoscaler: add safety margin to scale-down when shed_count crosses configured threshold. 3) Prefetch: adjust eviction heuristics to avoid simultaneous mass-eviction during shed events. 4) Run staged rollout on canary pool then dedicated pools and watch SLO metrics. Owner: runtime team (Lina Gomez). Target ETA: 2026-03-18.
follow_up_actions: Create PR to make shed handshake idempotent (owner: runtime)
Add automated e2e test that simulates mixed-priority load and asserts no 5xx floor when shed triggers (owner: infra/test)
Postmortem + timeline (owner: SRE) to be published in Confluence after incident is closed
